items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: For that wonderful celebration of my 50 years of trumpet, I also played a number with the choral, which was inspired as much by having me to play with them as I was hearing them sing.

ctx.x: We arrived at the city hall which is in France is called Hotel de Ville, and were greeted with the music played by a group of hunting players in their traditional costumes. The Mayor of Luneray, who is also a senator and the deputy of the country, which is called Seine Maritime, did the honour of making me the honorary citizen, and presented me with a certificate stating it's cause. I was obliged to make a speech which I can do on an occasion like that, about as well as I can walk on my hands, but I said…

After the ceremony, we went to the big potatoes storage plant where the festival always takes place. It was eleven in the morning, and we heard the choir of Luneray directed by Mrs Francoise Suplice, who also played organ. The choir was composed by about 40 people, and sang spirituals and many religious songs of the type one can only hear in a Negro baptist church. For that wonderful celebration of my 50 years of trumpet, I also played a number with the choral, which was inspired as much by having me to play with…

That day, I played with five different groups including a family group from England which had the mother player accordian, the father playing clarinet, the eldest son who was 15 at the time, played piano, a daughter, 11, was the singer, and it was really enjoyable to hear her singing 'I ain't gonna give nobody none of my jelly roll'. The youngest son plays trumpet and he was 9 years old. He did a good interpretation of Louis Armstrong, doing 'Sleepy time down South'. The name of the family is Tomasso. The father…
